Descriptive statistics from a survey design

Source: R/table_continuous_svy.R
table_continuous_svy.Rd

The design twin of table_continuous(): the same table of means, standard deviations, intervals and counts, computed from a survey::svydesign() or survey::as.svrepdesign() object instead of a data frame.

Not one statistic is computed here. survey::svymean() gives the mean, its standard error and its design effect, survey::svyvar() the standard deviation, survey::svyquantile() the quantiles, and survey::svyttest() / survey::regTermTest() / survey::svyranktest() the group comparison. Every interval and every test is referred to survey::degf(design).

Usage

table_continuous_svy(
  design,
  select = tidyselect::everything(),
  by = NULL,
  exclude = NULL,
  regex = FALSE,
  drop_na = TRUE,
  deff = FALSE,
  qrule = "math",
  df = NULL,
  test = c("welch", "student", "nonparametric"),
  p_value = NULL,
  p_adjust = "none",
  statistic = FALSE,
  show_n = TRUE,
  show_columns = NULL,
  ci = TRUE,
  labels = getOption("spicy.var_labels", FALSE),
  note_labels = NULL,
  ci_level = 0.95,
  digits = 2,
  p_digits = 3,
  decimal_mark = ".",
  align = c("decimal", "center", "right"),
  note = NULL,
  note_add = NULL,
  output = c("default", "data.frame", "long", "tinytable", "gt", "flextable", "excel",
    "clipboard", "word"),
  excel_path = NULL,
  excel_sheet = NULL,
  clipboard_delim = "\t",
  word_path = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  user_na = TRUE,
  style = NULL
)

Arguments

design

A survey design: survey::svydesign() or survey::as.svrepdesign(). Two-phase, pps, database-backed and multiframe designs are refused with a classed error.

select

Columns to summarize, as a tidyselect expression on the design's variables. As in table_continuous(), the by column is not part of the selection (naming it, or giving its position, is an error), a name that is not a column is an error, and so is a selection with no numeric column. The design's own columns are not part of it either, since they are not variables to describe: its sampling weights, replicate weights, cluster identifiers (every stage, unless each cluster of a one-stage design is a single observation) and finite population corrections. everything(), the other selection helpers and regex skip them, and naming one, or giving its position, is an error; table_continuous() describes it from the data. Strata stay variables, since a stratification variable such as a region is often one of interest. These columns are read from the design object. A design made by survey::as.svrepdesign() records none of them, and one made by survey::svrepdesign() names its sampling weights only in its call, as a formula, until subset(), update(), postStratify(), calibrate(), rake() or trimWeights() replaces the call: leave such a column out with a negation (select = !w).

by

A single grouping column. One domain per level, in the order of table_continuous(): a factor's levels, any other column sorted (text in the C locale, FALSE before TRUE, numbers ascending). A by that no observation holds is an error under drop_na = TRUE.

exclude

Columns to exclude. Supports tidyselect syntax and character vectors of column names.

regex

Logical. If FALSE (the default), uses tidyselect helpers. If TRUE, the select argument is treated as a regular expression.

drop_na

Drop observations with a missing by value. A table that computes removes the missing values by default and counts them in the note, the rule of table_continuous(): TRUE (the default) removes them, and the missing values of each summarized variable are always removed. The note lists both, by last: a missing by takes the observation out of the whole table, a missing value only out of its own variable. With FALSE they form a (Missing) domain of their own – an ordinary subpopulation, with its own degrees of freedom – which is excluded from the group comparison. Ignored (with a warning) when by is not used.

deff

Show the design effect: FALSE (default), TRUE (against sampling without replacement) or "replace" (against sampling with replacement, ignoring the finite population correction).

qrule

Quantile rule: "math" (default), "spicy", or anything survey::svyquantile() accepts, including a function.

df

Degrees of freedom for the intervals. NULL (default) uses survey::degf() on each domain. It does not reach the group comparison: survey::svyttest() and survey::svyranktest() have no df argument, so the test keeps the design's own degrees of freedom and the note says so.

test

Group comparison: "welch" (default), "student" (warns; identical under a design) or "nonparametric". A variable whose complete cases include negatively weighted rows is not compared: a design-based test is not defined when the weights change sign. Its estimates are still reported, the note says which comparisons were withheld, and the call warns (spicy_negative_weights_no_test).

p_value

Logical or NULL. If TRUE and by is used, adds a p-value column from the test specified by test. When NULL (the default), the p-value is shown automatically whenever by is supplied, and hidden otherwise. Pass p_value = FALSE to suppress the column explicitly. Ignored when by is not used.

p_adjust

Multiple-comparison adjustment of the p-value column, applied to the family of every test in the table (one design-based p-value per variable; a withheld test stays out). One of "none" (default), "holm", "hochberg", "hommel", "bonferroni", "BH" / "fdr", or "BY", as in table_regression(); delegated to stats::p.adjust(). Needs by and the p-value column. See Multiple-comparison adjustment.

statistic

Logical. If TRUE and by is used, the test statistic is shown in an additional column (e.g., t(df) = ..., F(df1, df2) = ..., W = ..., or H(df) = ...). Both p_value and statistic are independent; either or both can be enabled. Defaults to FALSE. Ignored when by is not used.

show_n

Logical. If TRUE, includes an unweighted n column in the printed ASCII table and in every rendered output (tinytable, gt, flextable, word, excel, clipboard). Set to FALSE to drop the n column structurally from those outputs (no empty placeholder, no spanner). The n column is always present in output = "long" for downstream programmatic access. Defaults to TRUE. Ignored (with a warning) when show_columns is supplied.

show_columns

Character vector of statistic tokens; NULL keeps the default display.

ci

Logical. If TRUE, includes the mean confidence interval columns (<level>% CI LL / <level>% CI UL) and their spanner in the printed ASCII table and in every rendered output (tinytable, gt, flextable, word, excel, clipboard). Set to FALSE to drop both columns and the CI spanner structurally from those outputs (no empty placeholders, no border lines under an empty header). The CI bounds are always present as ci_lower / ci_upper in output = "long" for downstream programmatic access. Defaults to TRUE. The CI level is taken from ci_level. Ignored (with a warning) when show_columns is supplied.

labels

How each variable is named in the table: in the rows, in the title, and in the notes. Four forms:

  • labels = FALSE shows the column name.

  • labels = TRUE shows the column's label attribute (as set by haven, labelled, or label_from_names()) when it is present, not NA, and not empty, and the column name otherwise.

  • labels = c(bmi = "Body mass index"), a named character vector, gives the columns it names these labels. Every other column follows options(spicy.var_labels): its name when the option is unset or FALSE, its label attribute when it is TRUE.

  • labels = var_labels(bmi = "BMI (kg/m2)") gives the columns it names these labels, and every other column its label attribute, whatever the option says. var_labels() alone is labels = TRUE.

A name that matches no column of the table warns (class spicy_unknown_name) and is left out, so one vector can still serve every table of a project. The default reads options(spicy.var_labels), and a TRUE or FALSE typed in the call wins over it. Any other value, NULL included, is an error. A variable label documents the data file; a published table carries the wording you set here. note_labels gives a variable a shorter label in the title and the notes.

note_labels

The label a variable takes where the table names it in a sentence, in the title and in the notes, in place of the one labels gives it: a named character vector, note_labels = c(sex = "sex at birth"), or a var_labels() object, which reads as one. labels can then name a row with a whole question while the note says "Missing values removed: sex at birth (2).". The rows, the column headers and the spanners keep the labels of labels, and so do the title and the notes for a variable note_labels does not name. A name that matches no column warns and is left out, as in labels, and NULL (the default) renames nothing. A note label that another variable of the table shows is an error (class spicy_label_collision): choose another one, or relabel the other variable.

ci_level

Confidence level for the mean confidence interval (default: 0.95): a number strictly between 0 and 1.

digits

Number of decimal places of the statistics on each variable's own scale: the mean, SD, standard error, median, IQR, quartiles, minimum and maximum, and the confidence interval of the mean. One non-negative whole number sets them for every variable (default: 2), and the weighted n and the design effect with them. A vector named by column, not by label, gives each variable it names its own, digits = c(height = 0, bmi = 1); the other variables, the weighted n and the design effect keep the default, the digits of a spicy_style() in force included. A name that matches no variable warns and is left out, as in labels. A fraction is an error, as for every *_digits argument. The p-values (p_digits), the test statistics (two decimals) and the counts keep their own decimals.

p_digits

Integer >= 1. Number of decimal places used to render p-values in the p column (default: 3, the APA Publication Manual standard). Both the displayed precision and the small-p threshold derive from this argument: p_digits = 3 prints .045 and <.001; p_digits = 4 prints .0451 and <.0001; p_digits = 2 prints .05 and <.01. Useful for genomics / GWAS contexts with very small p-values, or for journals using a coarser convention. Leading zeros are always stripped, following APA convention.

decimal_mark

The decimal mark, a single character: "." (the default) or "," in most styles; the Lancet style of spicy_style() uses the middle dot.

align

Horizontal alignment of numeric columns in the printed ASCII table and in the tinytable, gt, flextable, word, excel, and clipboard outputs. The first column (Variable) and Group (when present) are always left-aligned. One of:

  • "decimal" (default): align numeric columns on the decimal mark, the standard scientific-publication convention used by SPSS, SAS, and LaTeX siunitx. Numeric cells are pre-padded with figure-spaces (U+2007, digit-width) so every string in a column has the same width with the decimal mark at the same internal position; centering those uniform-width strings then stacks the decimal points vertically. The same pad-then-center strategy is applied on every rendering engine (gt, tinytable, flextable, word, ASCII print) for a homogeneous rendering, matching table_regression() and table_continuous_lm(). The clipboard output is delimited text meant to be parsed rather than read at a fixed width, so its cells travel unpadded (a padded number pastes as text next to an unpadded number).

  • "center": center-align all numeric columns.

  • "right": right-align all numeric columns.

"center" and "right" reach the excel output too. "decimal" does not: Excel cells are written unpadded, because cell-string padding does not align decimals under a proportional font, so the workbook keeps the engine's own convention instead – counts and the p-value right-aligned, the other numeric columns centered. Same default and same three values as table_continuous_lm(), whose excel output still uses that convention at every align.

note

The note under the table. NULL (the default) builds it: the general note, one paragraph opened by the lead-in of the style ("Note." by default, none under the jama and lancet themes; see note_label in spicy_style()), then, in a table_regression() with stars, the legend of the stars on a line of its own. A single string replaces the general note, the sentences the table writes about its data included. It is printed as typed, line breaks ("\n") included, after the lead-in of the style, which a string opening with a lead-in of its own does not repeat (note = "Note. Data weighted."), and the legend of the stars stays below it. "" keeps that legend alone, and no note at all without stars. FALSE removes the note from every output, the legend included.

note_add

Sentences to add to the note: a character vector of one or more strings, each printed as typed (no period is added) and joined to the note by a space. They close its paragraph, after the definitions of the abbreviations and before the legend of the stars, in every output and in attr(x, "note"), and the sentences the table writes stay. With a string in note, they follow it, so a wrapper can add a house sentence to every table while one table replaces its note. An NA or an empty string is an error, and so is note_add with note = FALSE, which leaves no note to add to.

output

One of "default", "data.frame", "long", or a rendering engine: "tinytable", "gt", "flextable", "excel", "clipboard", "word". "data.frame" is the displayed table with its numbers, "long" one row per (variable x group) with every statistic, as in table_continuous(); see Value.

excel_path

File path for output = "excel", ending in ".xlsx", in a directory that exists.

excel_sheet

Sheet name for output = "excel". NULL (the default) uses "Descriptives".

clipboard_delim

Delimiter for output = "clipboard" (default: "\t"). A cell holding the delimiter itself, a double quote or a line break is quoted RFC 4180-style, so the grid survives whatever delimiter you choose.

word_path

File path for output = "word", ending in ".docx", in a directory that exists.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, a message (class spicy_info) names the non-numeric columns left out (default: FALSE).

user_na

Logical. If TRUE (the default), declared missing values never reach the numeric summaries: they are excluded like NA and disclosed in the table note (Declared missing values removed: ...); declared-missing by values form no group. If FALSE, the declared codes are summarized as ordinary numbers. See the "Declared missing values" section of freq().

style

A journal style: a theme name ("jama", "nejm", "lancet", "annals", "apa", "aer"), a spicy_style() object, or NULL (the default). A style only changes DEFAULTS – any argument you pass explicitly wins over it. Set options(spicy.style = ) for document-wide scope. A theme covers numeric formatting, the word that opens the note and the abbreviations the note defines, not full editorial conformity; ?spicy_style lists the exact rules each one encodes and the official document they come from. An unknown name is an error.

Value

Depends on output:

  • "default": a spicy_continuous_svy_table (a data.frame subclass, with the parent class "spicy_table"), printed when the call is bare; its columns are the table's compute frame, and the display frame and the typed view are attached.

  • "data.frame": the displayed table with its numbers, what as.data.frame() of the default object returns: one row per printed row, the key columns variable, label and, with by, group and .row_role ("group", or "missing" for the group of missing by values), then the printed columns under their names ("M", "SD", "SE", "95% CI LL", ..., "n", "p"), as in table_continuous().

  • "long": one row per (variable x group) (per variable without by) with every statistic the table computes, whatever it displays: variable, label, group and .group_role (with by, as in table_continuous()), mean, sd, se, min, max, ci_lower, ci_upper, median, q1, q3, iqr, med_ci_lower, med_ci_upper, n (observed), weighted_n (the estimated population), deff, degf (the degrees of freedom of the domain), and, with by, the test on the first row of each variable: test_type ("design_t" or "design_f"), statistic, df, df.residual, p.value (with the p-value) and, under p_adjust, p_unadjusted.

  • "tinytable", "gt", "flextable": the rendered table.

  • "excel" / "word": writes the file and returns its path invisibly.

  • "clipboard": copies the table and returns the display data.frame invisibly.

The default object and the two data frames carry the whole note as printed, its lead-in included, in attr(x, "note"). The default object also keeps the title it prints in attr(x, "title").

Which function do I need?

A data frame with a column of weights is table_continuous() (weights = ). A survey design object – strata, clusters, finite population correction, calibration, replicate weights – is this function. Passing one to the other errors with the name of the right one; there is no silent coercion, because the design-based standard errors, degrees of freedom and tests cannot be recovered from the weights alone.

Two conventions, one bridge

table_continuous(weights = ) implements the frequency-expansion convention: a weight is a number of copies, and SD has denominator sum(w) - 1. This function implements the sampling-weight convention: a weight is a number of units represented, and SD is sqrt(survey::svyvar()), whose denominator is n - 1 on weights normalized to sum to n. These are two estimands, not two approximations of one.

rescale = TRUE is the bridge, and it is an identity rather than a coincidence. Writing w' = w * n / sum(w), the rescaled weighted variance is sum(w' (x - xbar)^2) / (sum(w') - 1) = n / (n - 1) * sum(w (x - xbar)^2) / sum(w), which is what survey::svyvar() computes. So on a design that declares nothing but weights, table_continuous(weights = w, rescale = TRUE) and this function return the same mean and the same standard deviation. The default rescale = FALSE does not, and that is the estimand boundary, not a bug.

The mean is continuous across both regimes: sum(w x) / sum(w) does not move when the weights are rescaled.

Choosing the statistics

show_columns takes the tokens of table_continuous() with two additions and one removal:

  • "se" – the design-based standard error of the mean;

  • "deff" – the design effect (requires deff = TRUE);

  • "med_ci" is refused. The exact interval of the sibling inverts a binomial sign test on independent observations, which a clustered or stratified sample is not.

Quantiles

qrule = "math" is the default and estimates inf{x : F(x) >= p}, the quantile of the population. qrule = "spicy" switches to the type-7 interpolation table_continuous() uses, for a reader who needs the two tables to agree cell for cell; any other value – including a function – is handed to survey::svyquantile() untouched. The note always says which rule produced the numbers.

Groups and degrees of freedom

by = cuts one domain per group with [ on the design. survey recomputes the degrees of freedom on the primary sampling units and strata each domain retains, so a grouped table generally carries a different df per row; the note gives the span when they differ.

A group with a missing value is a domain like any other: drop_na = FALSE gives it a (Missing) row, with its own degrees of freedom. A domain reduced to one primary sampling unit has none, and its interval shows the undefined dash rather than an interval built on qt(p, df = 0).

The comparison is a single test on the whole design, not a set of pairwise ones: survey::svyttest() with two observed groups, survey::regTermTest() on survey::svyglm() with three or more, or survey::svyranktest() under test = "nonparametric". Under a design the Welch / Student distinction does not exist – the variance is the design's – so test = "student" warns and behaves like "welch". A variable with no variance, or whose domains are each constant on their own value (a residual variance of zero), has no comparison, with a warning (class spicy_undefined_stat), where survey would still return a p-value. Under test = "nonparametric" too, unlike table_continuous(): survey::svyranktest() is a design-based test of the ranks, which are then constant within the domains as well. Its test cells show the undefined mark, as do those of any comparison that cannot run (too few observations in a domain, a test refused under weights that change sign). The note names the comparison of each variable.

A variable with no observed value in a domain (a question not asked in that group) has no data in it, as in table_continuous(): its cells there show an en dash, n included, those rows are not counted in the missing values of the note, the comparison uses the domains with data, and the note says so ("No data for X in G.").

Stability

This function is stabilizing in the sense ?spicy defines: the names of its design-specific arguments may still be tightened before 1.0 – with a NEWS.md entry – but the behavior does not change silently. It was experimental through 0.13; the shape of the table has held across the cycle, so it now moves on the parent family's clock rather than its own. The numbers themselves are survey's and do not move with it.

What is absent, and why

weights and rescale (the weighting is the design), effect_size and smd (no established design-based variance), and data.

Multiple-comparison adjustment

The p-values of a descriptive table describe: they test no prespecified hypothesis. STROBE (explanation of item 14) and the SAMPL guidelines advise against significance tests in descriptive and baseline tables, hence the default p_adjust = "none".

When a journal or a protocol asks for adjusted p-values anyway, p_adjust applies stats::p.adjust() to the family of every test in the table: one p-value per variable (one per block in table_outcome()), never the rows of one variable, which share one test. "holm" suits a confirmatory set of comparisons, "BH" a screening one; table_regression() lists the methods. A test that returned no p-value stays out of the family.

The adjustment runs before any formatting, so the p column and its <.001 threshold show the adjusted values, and the table note gives the number of tests and the method. The raw p-values stay in the object: a p_unadjusted column next to the p-value column of the returned data frames, and col_meta$p$p_unadjusted (with the method in p_adjust and the family size in p_adjust_m) in as_structured(). Without by, or with p_value = FALSE, the table shows no p-value to adjust, and a p_adjust other than "none" is an error.

See also

table_continuous() for the data-frame sibling, table_categorical_svy() for categorical variables, table_regression() on a survey::svyglm() fit for a model.

Examples

data(api, package = "survey")
dclus1 <- survey::svydesign(
  id = ~dnum, weights = ~pw, data = apiclus1, fpc = ~fpc
)
table_continuous_svy(dclus1, select = c(api00, api99))
#> Descriptive statistics
#> 
#>  Variable │   M       SD     Min     Max    95% CI LL  95% CI UL   n  
#> ──────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>  api00    │ 644.17  105.75  411.00  905.00   593.68     694.66    183 
#>  api99    │ 606.98  112.85  365.00  890.00   555.02     658.94    183 
#> 
#> Note. N = 183 (weighted 6194). Design: cluster (dnum), 15 PSU, with finite population correction; 14 degrees of freedom. Std. errors: Design-based (Taylor linearization). Confidence intervals and tests use the design degrees of freedom. CI = confidence interval; LL = lower limit; UL = upper limit.
table_continuous_svy(dclus1, select = api00, by = stype)
#> Descriptive statistics by stype
#> 
#>  Variable │ Group    M       SD     Min     Max    95% CI LL  95% CI UL   n  
#> ──────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>  api00    │ E      648.87  106.16  436.00  905.00   600.91     696.83    144 
#>           │ H      618.57   96.74  443.00  724.00   528.67     708.48     14 
#>           │ M      631.44  109.06  411.00  847.00   561.87     701.01     25 
#> 
#>  Variable │ Group   p   
#> ──────────┼─────────────
#>  api00    │ E      .314 
#>           │ H           
#>           │ M           
#> 
#> Note. N = 183 (weighted 6194). Design: cluster (dnum), 15 PSU, with finite population correction; degrees of freedom vary by group (7 to 14). Std. errors: Design-based (Taylor linearization). Confidence intervals and tests use the design degrees of freedom. P-value: design-based Wald test. The group comparison uses 12 degrees of freedom (observed groups only). CI = confidence interval; LL = lower limit; UL = upper limit.
table_continuous_svy(
  dclus1,
  select = api00,
  show_columns = c("m", "se", "ci", "deff", "n"),
  deff = TRUE
)
#> Descriptive statistics
#> 
#>  Variable   │    M        SE      95% CI LL    95% CI UL     n     DEff  
#> ────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>  api00      │  644.17    23.54     593.68       694.66      183    9.35  
#> 
#> Note. N = 183 (weighted 6194). Design: cluster (dnum), 15 PSU, with finite population correction; 14 degrees of freedom. Std. errors: Design-based (Taylor linearization). Confidence intervals and tests use the design degrees of freedom. SE = design-based standard error of the mean; CI = confidence interval; LL = lower limit; UL = upper limit; DEff = design effect.
